title: VESPER Context Fragment
description: REM-003 §4.4-4.5. Every piece of content entering a model context is a fragment carrying a trust class, and the context ceiling is the minimum over all of them. Taint propagates through summarisation, embedding and cache reuse -- that single sentence is the whole defence against unattended overnight research with shell and comms access, and it is the one an implementation omits, because summarisation naturally produces a clean-looking new string. Authority: SR-025, SR-054; INV-AUTH-3/6/7; CI-012, CI-014.

trust_class.description: Maps to allowed_level for STATE-CHANGING capabilities: system L5, owner L5, verified_local L4, retrieved_local L3, model_generated L2, retrieved_external L1. context_ceiling = min over all fragments in context.

context_role.description: REM-003 §4.5, the two-context research pattern. `planner` holds full authority; `extraction` holds L1 and no state-changing tools and must emit schema-validated output.

derived_from.description: Fragment ids this one was derived from. A summary, an embedding, or a cache hit MUST list its inputs: `trust_class` is then the WEAKEST of them, computed rather than declared. This array is what CI-012 follows to prove taint survived the summariser.

cache_tier.description: SR-054's five tiers. Present here rather than only in the cache subsystem because a cache entry INHERITS the taint of what it caches (GAP-027) -- a clean-looking prefix cache is otherwise a laundering path straight into the planner context.

sensitive.description: Secrets are never fragments. This flag marks content that must not reach telemetry (INV-OBS-1); it is not a mechanism for admitting secrets into context.

then.$comment: INV-AUTH-6 as a schema property: a retrieved_external fragment CANNOT carry context_role planner. The high-authority planner context never ingests raw external content -- injected instructions cannot survive schema validation into a field the planner treats as an instruction, because no such field exists.

A summary, embedding or cache entry with no declared inputs is malformed. Without this, the natural implementation returns a fresh untainted string and the ceiling silently rises -- the exact build A-025's negative control must be shown failing against.
The extraction context is the one that ingests hostile content. Nothing sensitive is placed in it.

$comment: EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: any `trusted: true` override field, and any way to set trust_class higher than the minimum of derived_from. Taint is monotone downward; there is no sanitisation operation, because a sanitiser is a thing an attacker writes input for.
